reasoning: The evidence shows the Penal Bill passed its first reading in November 2025 (39-16 vote). Multiple sources from January-February 2026 indicate it is currently under review by the National Security Committee, pending second and third readings. As of the forecast date (March 6, 2026), with only ~26 days until April 1, 2026, the bill has not yet passed second and third readings. While the bill has strong coalition support and Ben-Gvir's backing, no sources indicate imminent passage of the remaining readings. The legislative process typically requires time between readings, and no specific dates for second/third readings are mentioned in recent reports. The bill faces significant international opposition and some domestic criticism, though opposition parties appear weak. Given the tight timeline and lack of evidence of scheduled votes, passage by April 1 appears unlikely but not impossible.
